model.name: The Cool People's
model.notes: In the openpilot 0.10.1 tag; named in the 0.10.3 release notes. Same vision model as North Nevada (2cc530ac/500), new policy fd9a6816/400. Plan only, commands from modeld's get_action_from_model.

public_open_loop.condition: Measured. comma's public two-camera segments (openpilot CI data), native intrinsics and the device's own calibration, both cameras; every model on the same decoded frames. Truth is what the recording car did next: carState speed and acceleration, yaw rate from the device's cameraOdometry. Segments where the car never moves have no data. 39 of the 45 listed segments have a score, from 23 drives and 20 cars.

metrics.label: Lateral error at the model's own best lead
Lateral correlation with the car's later motion
Lateral gain (1 = same size as the car's motion)
Lead of the lateral request over the car's motion

public_closed_loop.condition: Measured. comma's worldmodel-4B generates each next frame at 5 Hz from 9 history frames, 5 recorded anchor frames and the car's pose; the model drives comma's ideal car (the requested curvature and acceleration happen at once) for 7.2 s from the recorded start. Distance is to the recording car's own path. One window per segment, nearest the middle, where the car holds at least 5 m/s for the window and the 4.8 s before it; segments with no such stretch are left out. Seeds 0 and 1, averaged per segment.

truck_open_loop.condition: Measured. The G55's recorded drives replayed through the model with both of the truck's cameras (each setup's own wide-camera calibration), road-plane warp to 1.45 m. Where the narrow lens does not cover comma's narrow view (the 8 mm lens in the V13 case), those pixels come from the wide camera, brightness matched. Truth is the truck's CAN speed and yaw rate. 30 s windows after a 5 s warm-up; window = unit, drive = cluster; results are also given per camera setup. Corpus windows of 30 s from the truck's recorded drives, scored per camera setup.

metrics.label: Lateral error at the model's own best lead
Lateral correlation with the car's later motion
Lateral gain (1 = same size as the car's motion)
Lead of the lateral request over the car's motion

truck_closed_loop.condition: Measured. worldmodel-4B as in the public closed loop, but the model drives a simulation of the G55's measured steering and powertrain response instead of the ideal car. Lane-following windows from the G55's drives, day and night; distance is to the driver's recorded path; seeds 0 and 1, averaged per window.

truck_recovery.condition: Measured. The truck closed loop with a disturbance while the model drives; only the tests listed ran.

limits: Open-loop scores compare a model's action with what the recording driver or car did; a model that drives differently but well is scored as wrong. comma's RL residual makes the lateral action smoother, and earlier than its base's by 0.10 to 0.26 s (measured on the G55 and on 16 of comma's cars); both score as error here. Measured on the 2026-10-27 deep dive: open-loop accuracy did not predict closed-loop driving.

Closed-loop numbers come from a generative world model, not a car. In a separate test on the G55's windows, worldmodel-4B followed an added yaw command through 2 s but showed 0 to 20% of an added lateral offset 3 to 4 s later; past about 4 s the recorded anchor frames also pull every model back toward the recorded path. The front-page ranking uses 2 s.

Intervals are 95% percentile bootstraps that resample whole drives (the drive a public segment was cut from, the recorded drive a truck window comes from), so segments of one drive count once. Below 10 drives there is no interval: the truck sections come from fewer drives and report means and win counts only.
Paired deltas are model minus baseline on the units both have (for lateral gain, the change in its distance from 1); wins count units where the model is better in the metric's direction.

The lead of the lateral request is the shift, searched from 0 to 1.5 s, at which the request best correlates with the car's later lateral motion; a larger value means the request comes earlier. A value at either edge is censored and left out. Plan speed error at 3 s reads the plan head, which does not separate models built on one frozen base: it is identical on every segment for the four f22e06e5 models, and for Cinque v2 and v3.

Truck open loop comes from few drives, and the camera setup changed between them (lens, housing, aim); the pooled number mixes setups, so read the per-setup numbers too. The 8 mm setups' wide camera recorded about 7-10 fps, so its frame can be up to ~60 ms from the narrow one. On the V14 setup up to 7 of a window's 700 steps are ~100 ms (one camera frame dropped). The camera's aim is the truck's live calibration learned on each drive; drives whose recorded calibration was carried over from another drive are left out.

A historical model, run outside comma's software with its own release's inputs, camera warp and command (engines/legacy.py). Checked against comma's CI model replay of this model (made on a comma device, 60 frames of one route): the plan's lateral position is 0.032 m RMS from comma's output; every other model here is 0.67 m or more from it on the same check.

Trained for the comma devices and cameras of its time, not for the G55's camera or for every camera among comma's public segments: of those 45 segments 26 record the OX03C10 sensor, 6 the AR0231, 4 the OS04C10 and 9 none; 30 were recorded 2021 to 2024 and 15 come from devices whose route names carry no date.
Not run in closed loop: the G55 closed-loop and recovery tests need this release's controller inside the world-model loop, which is not built yet.

The commands are 0.10's modeld (get_action_from_model on the plan, lateral delay = steer actuator delay + 0.2 s, smoothed over 0.1 s lateral and 0.3 s longitudinal); the newest models are scored on their own unsmoothed action head, so lateral action rates are not comparable across these eras.
